name: worker-preclaim-qualification
goal: Leave tasks queued when provider isolation is unqualified and retain the launch-time qualification check.

evidence: An unqualified default worker can claim and mark a task failed before its launcher rejects; it should reject without changing the task ref and should still recheck qualification at launch.

The existing aborted-preclaim and context-failure worker case checks cancellation but never tests default runner qualification before claiming; extend that same class-method case to assert an unchanged queue and zero context calls.
Committed test-only 56f4737569; guarded clean-snapshot run on harbor-mbp-2 recorded failing assertion instead of rejecting, proof da800b9424a834af6a31c60051da64bbc7e4f1ac37811c3630e474653b56ba5e.
At 36075e5b14 the worker awaits trusted runner readiness before owner lookup and task claim; the launch adapter still rechecks qualification before sandbox preparation or provider execution.

The unchanged focused case passed on harbor-mbp-2 at 36075e5b14 under the same sanitized runtime and environment; green proof 1eb920eae22150b32c9774c062daa7e70e5091f54f8450312d5040570114228b, red proof da800b9424a834af6a31c60051da64bbc7e4f1ac37811c3630e474653b56ba5e.
